source_ref.product: 토스증권 주식투자 앱의 주식 커뮤니티 기능 (Toss Securities stock-investing app — stock community feature)
source_ref.production_note: 40s music-only kinetic-typography product film for Toss Securities' stock community feature. No live action, no narration. Pure motion-graphics on alternating white and black backgrounds with brand blue accent (~#3182F6). Opens with a stacked speech-bubble montage dramatizing the pain point of fragmented Korean stock communities (각 말풍선이 아래에서 위로 쌓임), pivots to a black kinetic-type question card, then enumerates four named features in white title cards — 인기글 알림, 투표 기능, 주주배지, MAU 120만 — each animating a simplified 3D phone mockup / UI vignette, and closes with two black brand-statement cards and a clean white toss securities logo endcard. On-screen copy builds: 주식 초보인데 정보 좀 주실 분? / 잘 산 건지 궁금한데 물어볼 곳이 없네.. / 다들 진짜 주주는 맞나? 마음 편히 소통하고 싶다... / 주식 커뮤니티, 종토방 말고는 없는 거야? // 우리에게 필요한 커뮤니티는? // 주식 초보도 쉽게 의견을 나눌 수 있고 신뢰할 만한 새로운 주식 커뮤니티 // 토스증권에 있습니다 // 인기글 알림 — 관심 있는 종목에 대한 그날의 정보를 알려드려요 // 투표 기능 — 많은 사람들의 의견을 한눈에 볼 수 있어요 // 주주배지 — 주주가 쓴 글이 75%! 믿고 볼 수 있어요 // MAU 120만 — 요즘 눈에 띄게 활발한 주식 커뮤니티 // 주식 커뮤니티를 보는 새로운 시선 / 주식 커뮤니티 누구나 누릴 수 있게. A persistent legal disclaimer ticker scrolls along the bottom edge through the feature section.

target_demo: Korean retail investors, especially beginner and casual stock investors in their 20s-40s seeking a trustworthy place to discuss stocks
narrative_arc: problem_montage → question_pivot → solution_thesis → feature_1 → feature_2 → feature_3 → feature_4 → brand_statement → logo_endcard

production_signature.signature_note: No physical camera; everything is composited motion graphics. Signature look is the Toss design language: ultra-clean white or pure-black canvas, generous negative space, bold rounded Korean sans-serif, a single brand-blue accent used to spotlight the operative keyword in each line, and friendly simplified 3D objects (phone, ballot box) rendered with soft studio shadows. Transitions between feature cards are soft text fades/slides rather than hard cuts, so the white-background feature section reads as one continuous canvas even as content swaps. Hard cuts occur only at the white↔black background changes.

global_layout.layout_note: Two recurring layouts: (1) full-screen centered kinetic type on black for thesis/question/brand cards; (2) white feature card with a blue feature-name title near the top, a simplified 3D phone/UI vignette in the center, and a two-line black subhead near the bottom. A small grey legal-disclaimer ticker runs along the very bottom edge through the feature section. Brand blue (#3182F6) consistently highlights the single key noun/verb of each copy line.

Brand blue spotlights the operative keyword in nearly every line for scannability.

audio.audio_note: Music-only spot. faster_whisper returned zero speech segments (speech_coverage 0.0) and visual inspection confirms there is no spoken narration — every message is delivered through on-screen kinetic typography only. Soundtrack is a light, upbeat brand BGM bed with likely subtle UI/whoosh SFX accenting the type and mockup animations. All copy lines are captions/on-screen text, not voice-over.

shots.pose_description: On a pure white canvas, light grey rounded speech-bubble cards build one at a time from the bottom of the frame upward into a vertical stack. Each bubble carries a small username (Forest, Stelil, Richman, Melooo), a relative timestamp (5시간 전, 3시간 전, 1시간 전, 35분 전), a colorful emoji avatar, and a two-line Korean message in bold dark sans-serif. By the end up to four bubbles are stacked center-frame.

recreation_prompts.t2i_start_frame: A clean minimalist motion-graphics still on a pure white seamless background, rendered in the friendly flat design language of a modern Korean fintech app. Centered in the lower-middle of the 16:9 frame is a vertical stack of two to four rounded-rectangle speech-bubble cards, each in a very pale neutral grey fill with soft rounded corners (approximately 24px radius) and a gentle diffuse drop shadow that lifts them slightly off the white field. Each card has a small downward speech-tail at its lower-left corner. Inside each card, the top row shows a small username in a medium-weight dark grey Korean sans-serif (for example Forest, Stelil, Richman, Melooo) followed by a lighter grey relative timestamp (for example 5시간 전, 3시간 전, 1시간 전, 35분 전). To the left of the message sits a colorful round emoji avatar — a person-raising-hand emoji, a leaf emoji, a pair of eyes emoji, a fairy emoji — adding small warm pops of orange, green and blue to the otherwise neutral palette. Below the header, each card carries a two-line message in bold near-black Korean sans-serif: the first card reads 주식 초보인데 / 정보 좀 주실 분?, the second reads 잘 산 건지 궁금한데 / 물어볼 곳이 없네.., the third reads 다들 진짜 주주는 맞나? / 마음 편히 소통하고 싶다..., the fourth reads 주식 커뮤니티, / 종토방 말고는 없는 거야?. The composition uses very generous white negative space above the stack, with the cards occupying roughly the bottom 55 percent of the frame, conveying that more messages keep arriving from below. The typography is crisp, high-legibility, and humanist with rounded terminals, characteristic of Toss-style Korean UI. Lighting is flat, even, high-key, with no gradients on the background and only the faintest soft shadow beneath each card to imply layering. The overall color grade is bright, clean, neutral, and unsaturated except for the small emoji glyphs. The mood is one of relatable everyday frustration — ordinary retail investors voicing that they have nowhere trustworthy to ask questions or discuss stocks. There are no real logos, no real photographs, and no real identifiable people; the avatars are generic system emoji and the usernames are invented handles. The aesthetic anchor is a clean 4K Korean commercial motion-graphic frame: vector-flat, app-native, friendly, premium-minimal, with perfect kerning and pixel-snapped alignment. The cards are horizontally centered on a single vertical axis and vertically distributed with consistent gaps, building a tidy column. This frame is the opening problem-statement hook of a Toss Securities stock-community feature ad, establishing the pain point that Korean stock investors lack a comfortable, credible community, expressed entirely through stacked chat-bubble copy in the brand's signature clean white-canvas style with bold Korean sans-serif and isolated emoji color accents. Korean culture context: 종토방 refers to the often-toxic legacy stock message boards, which the copy contrasts against the desire for a calmer place to talk. The render should feel like a single keyframe from a tasteful, restrained kinetic-typography sequence. To elaborate the construction for faithful reproduction: the white field should be a perfectly even paper-white with no vignette and no off-white tint, so the cards appear to float in clean studio space. Each speech-bubble card has a consistent internal padding of roughly twenty-eight pixels, a one-line header and a two-line body, and the body text uses a slightly larger weight than the header for hierarchy. The gap between stacked cards is uniform, around thirty-two pixels, and the entire column is optically centered rather than mathematically centered so it feels balanced to the eye. The emoji avatars are small, roughly forty-eight pixels in diameter, positioned to the left of the message body and vertically centered against the two text lines. The timestamps are deliberately muted grey so they recede and let the bold black messages dominate. The lowest card in the stack sits a comfortable margin above the bottom edge, leaving room for more bubbles to arrive, and the topmost card has begun to drift toward the upper-middle of the frame, implying scroll. The shadows beneath the cards are very soft, low-opacity, and offset only a few pixels downward, never harsh. There is a faint sense of depth as newer cards overlap slightly in front of older ones. The composition should read instantly as a stylized, idealized chat or community feed — warm, human, and a little anxious in content but impeccably calm in design — exactly the tension the brand wants to resolve. Every Korean character is rendered with consistent stroke contrast and the punctuation marks (the question marks and ellipses) are clearly legible, since they carry the emotional tone of each message. This is the establishing problem frame and must look effortless, premium, and unmistakably in the modern Korean fintech motion-graphics idiom.
recreation_prompts.t2i_negative: photograph, real people, real brand logos, 3d realism, dark background, heavy gradients, clutter, neon, grunge texture, watermark
recreation_prompts.i2v_motion: Speech-bubble cards enter one at a time, each rising up from below the bottom edge and settling into the stack with a gentle ease-out and a tiny overshoot, pushing earlier cards slightly upward to make room. Soft shadows update as cards layer. The whole column drifts upward very subtly as the fourth bubble lands. Light, friendly pacing synced to upbeat BGM; no camera move. Roughly 6 seconds, ending on a hard cut to a black kinetic-type card.
recreation_prompts.fidelity_note: craft-faithful; on-screen Korean copy preserved verbatim; avatars generic emoji; no real identities or logos

shots.pose_description: Full black canvas. White bold Korean sans-serif appears in two centered lines — first 우리에게 필요한, then the second line 커뮤니티는? in which the word 커뮤니티 is colored brand blue while the question particle 는? stays white. The line reads as a rhetorical question: what kind of community do we actually need?

recreation_prompts.t2i_start_frame: A bold, minimalist kinetic-typography still on a pure solid black background filling the entire 16:9 frame, in the clean modern style of a premium Korean fintech brand film. Centered horizontally and vertically is a two-line Korean headline set in a heavy rounded sans-serif typeface with excellent legibility and generous letter spacing. The first line reads 우리에게 필요한 in pure white. The second line, directly beneath it and tightly leaded, reads 커뮤니티는? — and within this line the word 커뮤니티 is rendered in a vivid brand blue (approximately #3182F6, the Toss blue), while the trailing grammatical particle 는 and the question mark ? remain white. The blue keyword pops crisply against the black field, drawing the eye to the operative concept of community. There is nothing else in the frame: no images, no logos, no decoration, only the two lines of type surrounded by vast black negative space, which gives the message gravity and focus. The type is perfectly centered on a single vertical axis, with the two lines forming a compact rhetorical question that asks, in effect, what kind of community do we actually need. The contrast between the pure white text, the saturated blue keyword, and the deep black background is extremely high, making the frame feel deliberate, confident, and a little dramatic — a pause-and-reflect beat after the noisy stack of complaint bubbles that preceded it. The rendering is flat and vector-clean with no gradients, no grain, no glow other than the inherent crispness of the glyphs, and no texture; it should look like a single keyframe pulled from a restrained, high-end motion-graphics sequence. The Korean glyphs are humanist with rounded terminals and even stroke weight, pixel-snapped and beautifully kerned. The mood is anticipatory and clarifying: the ad has just dramatized the problem and now poses the central question it intends to answer. No real people, no photographs, no third-party brand marks appear. The aesthetic anchor is a clean 4K Korean commercial title card: black canvas, bold Korean sans-serif, one brand-blue accent word, total typographic minimalism. Korean culture context: the line uses the inclusive first-person plural 우리에게 (for us), a warm rhetorical framing common in Korean advertising that invites the viewer to feel addressed personally. The keyframe should sit at the moment both lines are fully visible and settled, the blue keyword at full saturation. For faithful reproduction, note the precise construction: the black background must be a true deep black, edge to edge, with no gradient, no vignette, and no texture, so the type appears to hover in pure void. The two lines are tightly leaded, with the second line sitting close beneath the first to read as a single connected thought rather than two separate statements. The white of the non-keyword text is a clean pure white, not cream, and the blue keyword is a saturated, slightly cool brand blue with crisp anti-aliased edges and no glow halo. Letter spacing is generous but not loose, optimized for on-screen legibility at broadcast scale, and the glyph weight is heavy enough to hold presence against the vast black field without becoming clumsy. The line block is optically centered both horizontally and vertically, occupying only a small fraction of the total frame so that the surrounding black negative space does most of the dramatic work. The question mark at the end of the second line is clearly formed and sits tight against the final syllable, carrying the rhetorical weight of the line. There is a deliberate, confident stillness to the frame — this is a breath, a pivot beat, the visual equivalent of a pause before an answer. Nothing competes with the type: no decorative lines, no underlines, no icons, no progress dots, no captions, no watermark. The overall impression is of restraint and intention, a single clean question floating in black, which is exactly how premium Korean fintech brand films stage their key turning-point copy. The keyframe must look like a deliberately art-directed title card rather than a default text overlay, with perfect kerning and pixel-snapped baselines.

recreation_prompts.i2v_motion: Line one 우리에게 필요한 fades up and rises a few pixels into place; a beat later line two 커뮤니티는? fades in beneath it, and the keyword 커뮤니티 shifts from white to brand blue with a quick, clean color pop. Text holds, perfectly still, on black. No camera movement. About 2 seconds, ending on a hard cut to a white card.

shots.pose_description: The white canvas returns; the stacked complaint bubbles shrink and recede, then the brand thesis builds in centered black Korean type with blue keyword highlights: 주식 초보도 [쉽게] / [의견]을 나눌 수 있고 / [신뢰]할 만한 / 새로운 [주식 커뮤니티]. recreation_prompts.t2i_start_frame: A clean high-key motion-graphics still on a pure white background in the friendly minimalist style of a Korean fintech brand film, capturing a transitional beat where the earlier cluster of grey complaint speech-bubbles has shrunk down and is receding toward the center-distance while the brand's solution thesis assembles as centered kinetic typography. The dominant element is a stack of centered Korean headline lines in bold near-black rounded sans-serif, with selected operative words highlighted in vivid brand blue (approximately #3182F6). The copy reads, across four short centered lines: 주식 초보도 쉽게 (with 쉽게 in blue), then 의견을 나눌 수 있고 (with 의견 in blue), then 신뢰할 만한 (with 신뢰 in blue), then a slightly separated final line 새로운 주식 커뮤니티 (with 주식 커뮤니티 in blue). The blue keywords spotlight the promise: easy, opinion-sharing, trustworthy, a new stock community. Around and behind the type there is generous white negative space. Along the very bottom edge of the frame runs a thin, small, light-grey legal disclaimer ticker in tiny Korean type (regulatory boilerplate such as 투자전 설명 청취 및 상품설명서/약관 필독 and 이 금융상품은 예금자보호법에 따라 보호되지 않습니다), partially visible and quietly scrolling, as is standard in Korean financial advertising. The lighting is flat, even, and bright with no gradients on the background and only the faintest soft shadow beneath any residual card shapes. The color grade is clean, neutral, and unsaturated except for the brand-blue keywords. The mood is reassuring and optimistic — having posed the problem and the question, the ad now answers with a calm, confident promise of a better stock community. The composition is strictly centered on a single vertical axis with consistent line spacing, conveying order and trustworthiness. The Korean glyphs are humanist, rounded, evenly weighted, pixel-snapped and beautifully kerned, exactly in the Toss UI typographic tradition. There are no real photographs, no real people, and no third-party brand logos; any residual bubble cards are generic neutral shapes. The aesthetic anchor is a clean 4K Korean commercial frame: white canvas, bold Korean sans-serif, isolated brand-blue accent words, and a discreet legal ticker. Korean culture context: the inclusive, gentle phrasing (초보도, 누구나-style accessibility) reflects the brand's positioning of finance as approachable for beginners, a recurring theme in Korean fintech marketing. The keyframe should depict the moment all four thesis lines are present with their blue keywords saturated and the bubble cluster reduced to a small receding accent. For faithful reproduction, observe the layout discipline: the four lines are vertically stacked with comfortable, even spacing, the final line 새로운 주식 커뮤니티 set slightly apart with a touch more space above it to mark it as the conclusion of the build. The blue keywords are placed at the start or within each line exactly where the eye lands first, so a quick scan of just the blue words communicates the whole promise — easy, opinion, trust, new stock community. The white background is pure and even with no tint, and the dark body text is a near-black charcoal rather than pure black, which reads as softer and friendlier on white, consistent with the brand's warm minimalism. The receding complaint bubbles, if shown, are small, slightly transparent, and clustered toward the center-distance, clearly subordinate to the type and on their way out of frame. The bottom legal ticker is genuinely tiny, single-line, light grey, and runs the full width of the frame, the kind of fast-scrolling regulatory text Korean viewers visually filter out but which must be present for compliance authenticity. The composition leaves generous breathing room on the left and right margins so the centered type feels uncrowded. Every glyph is crisp, evenly weighted, and pixel-snapped, and the blue is the same consistent brand blue used elsewhere in the film, tying the visual language together. The overall feeling is calm reassurance arriving after noise — the design itself models the very promise of a cleaner, more trustworthy community. The keyframe must look like a polished motion-graphics beat, not a slide, with intentional kerning, balanced color rhythm, and a clear reading order from top to bottom.
